instruction: Integrate the extension package '/home/user/test.vsix' into Visual Studio Code.

metadata.explanation: Using 'integrate' as action verb. Same verification approach as original.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical logical issue: The command uses pipe operator '|' in an array format without 'shell: true' parameter
The vm_command_line getter defaults to shell=False (general.py:12), which means the pipe will be treated as a literal argument, not a shell pipe operator
This will cause the command to fail at runtime - it will try to execute 'code --list-extensions' with literal arguments '|', 'grep', 'undefined_publisher.test' instead of piping the output to grep
The evaluator logic is otherwise correct - checking if 'undefined_publisher.test' is in the list of installed extensions is the right approach for verifying VSCode extension installation
The expected value 'undefined_publisher.test' appears semantically correct for a .vsix file named 'test.vsix' with undefined publisher
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add 'shell': true to the result config in the evaluator: {"type": "vm_command_line", "command": [...], "shell": true}

Alternatively, simplify the command to just ["code", "--list-extensions"] without the grep, and let the metric check if the extension ID is contained in the full output (which already happens with the 'contain' rule type)
